# Candidate Show HN post

Title: Show HN: KeibiDrop – Work on remote large files on-demand (no upload/download)
Project URL: https://github.com/KeibiSoft/KeibiDrop/
Posted (UTC): 2026-10-21T13:06:09Z

## Project page text (fetch status: ok)

```text
Website
·
Download
·
Blog
Open files on another computer without downloading them first
Mac to Windows, one folder, nothing to download first.
Two computers side by side. Click to watch on YouTube, with sound.
Another computer's files show up as a folder on yours, and you open and edit them in your own apps with nothing to download first.
A big file opens right away, because only the parts you read cross the network, and your edits save back.
No cloud stores your files, and the relay that connects you cannot read them, because they are end-to-end encrypted with protection against future quantum computers.
On the same network you connect with one click. Over the internet you swap a code once and then save the contact.
With Teleport on, your friend's files are a real folder on your computer, so any app works with them,
git clone
included.
It runs on macOS, Linux, Windows and Android, and iOS is on the way. The code is open source under the AGPL-3.0.
Get it:
Mac
·
Windows
·
Linux
·
Android
·
every click, per computer
· or
try it on the web
Jump to:
Install
·
Quick start
·
Direct transfer and Teleport
·
NAS
·
Encryption
·
By trade
·
Troubleshooting
Getting started:
install it on both computers and connect once. On the same Wi-Fi, turn on Local mode; anywhere else, send your code in any chat and paste your friend's code. Then drop a file in, or open their files with Teleport. Each step has a
short clip
, and the clips are also a
YouTube playlist
. To open the files on a NAS or a home server, see
Run it on a NAS
.
Copy your code, send it in any chat, paste your friend's code, and both of you press Connect.
With direct transfer, you drag files in and your friend saves the ones they need.
With Teleport, your friend's files appear as a folder that any app can open.
Finder shows the Teleport Folder like any other folder.
git works inside the Teleport Folder.
Install
macOS
brew tap keibisoft/keibidrop
brew trust keibisoft/keibidrop
brew install keibidrop
Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)
wget -O keibidrop.deb
$(
curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/KeibiSoft/KeibiDrop/releases/latest \
|
grep -o
'
https://[^"]*_amd64\.deb
'
)
sudo apt install ./keibidrop.deb
Windows
choco install keibidrop
Or download from
GitHub Releases
.
Android
We host our own F-Droid repository. Open
fdroid.keibisoft.com
on your phone, scan the code, and check the fingerprint before you add it.
To add it by hand, use
https://fdroid.keibisoft.com/fdroid/repo
in F-Droid under Settings, Repositories. The fingerprint to check is on the same page.
NAS or home server
On Unraid, open the Apps tab and search for KeibiDrop in Community Applications. On Synology Container Manager, QNAP Container Station or any other Docker host, use
keibisoft/keibidrop
from Docker Hub, or
ghcr.io/keibisoft/keibidrop
. The setup is in
Run it on a NAS
.
Build from source
git clone https://github.com/KeibiSoft/KeibiDrop.git
cd
KeibiDrop
make build-kd
#
CLI daemon
make build-cli
#
Interactive CLI
make build-rust
#
Desktop UI (needs Rust + Slint)
Quick start
On the same network:
You and your friend both open KeibiDrop and turn on Local mode.
Your computers find each other.
Click your friend's computer to connect.
Share files.
Over the internet:
You and your friend both open KeibiDrop.
Copy your code and send it to your friend in any chat.
Paste each other's codes and both press Connect.
Share files.
Save your friend as a contact to skip the code exchange next time.
KeibiDrop works through firewalls. When a direct connection fails, it uses an encrypted relay, so you need no port forwarding and no router setup.
Direct transfer and Teleport
With direct transfer you add files and your friend saves the ones they need. It needs nothing extra and suits sending large files.
With Teleport your friend's files appear as a folder on your computer, which suits working on shared files and git repositories. It needs a driver installed once:
macFUSE
on a Mac,
fuse3
on Linux or
WinFsp
on Windows.
Run it on a NAS
A NAS or a home server stays online, so it can serve a folder to your computer all the time. The box runs the KeibiDrop container. Your computer opens the box's folder with Teleport, from anywhere, and reads only what it opens.
On your computer, install KeibiDrop and the Teleport driver. Open the app, keep Local mode off and press
Copy my code
.
On the box, save
docker-compose.yml
, set the folder to share and paste your computer's code into
KD_PEER
.
Run
docker compose up -d
, then
docker compose logs -f
. The log prints the box's code.
On your computer, turn on
Teleport
, paste the box's code and press
Connect
.
Press
Save contact
and turn on
Auto
on the contact's row. From then on both sides reconnect by themselves.
The box's files now show in your Teleport Folder,
~/KeibiDrop/Mount
by default. Open the files from there in any app. For DaVinci Resolve, follow the
Resolve setup
.
The image is on Docker Hub as
keibisoft/keibidrop
and on GHCR as
ghcr.io/keibisoft/keibidrop
, for amd64 and arm64, and Unraid installs it from Community Applications. The container's settings and the limits are in
docker/README.md
, and the full guide is
Run KeibiDrop on a NAS
.
Connection and encryption
The two computers exchange codes, or find each other on the local network.
KeibiDrop picks the fastest path: the local network, a direct connection or the encrypted relay.
Files cross an encrypted channel that the relay cannot read.
Keys rotate during the session for forward secrecy.
The encryption is post-quantum (ML-KEM-1024 + X25519) with AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305. Full protocol details in
Security.md
.
Interfaces
Desktop UI
(Rust/Slint)
./keibidrop
Interactive CLI
(terminal REPL)
./keibidrop-cli
Agent CLI
(for scripts and AI agents, all output is JSON)
./kd start
#
Start daemon
./kd show fingerprint
#
Get your fingerprint
./kd register
<
peer-fingerprint
>
#
Register peer
./kd create
#
Create room (or: kd join)
./kd add /path/to/file.zip
#
Share a file
./kd list
#
List shared files
./kd pull file.zip
~
/Downloads/
#
Download a file
See
docs/kd-agent-guide.md
.
Configuration
KeibiDrop reads
~/.config/keibidrop/config.toml
. Environment variables override the config.
Setting
Env var
Default
Relay server
KD_RELAY
https://keibidroprelay.keibisoft.com/
Bridge relay
KD_BRIDGE
bridge.keibisoft.com:26600
Save folder
KD_SAVE_PATH
~/KeibiDrop/Received/
Teleport Folder
KD_MOUNT_PATH
~/KeibiDrop/Mount/
Inbound port
KD_INBOUND_PORT
26431
Teleport off
KD_NO_FUSE
false
Security
Post-quantum hybrid key exchange prevents future quantum computers from decrypting recorded traffic. Forward secrecy via periodic re-keying limits exposure if a session key is ever compromised.
By default, identity persists across sessions (so saved contacts keep working), encrypted with a per-install master key stored in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain Services, Linux Secret Service, Windows Credential Manager). Headless setups fall back to
~/.config/keibidrop/.master.key
(mode 0600). A passphrase (Argon2id) can protect it for users who back up the config to a cloud. Incognito mode uses a new key pair for each session and writes nothing to disk, so two sessions cannot be linked.
Full protocol description:
Security.md
Troubleshooting
See
TROUBLESHOOTING.md
.
Contributing
See
CONTRIBUTING.md
.
License
From version 0.5.0 the engine, CLI, mobile bindings and desktop UI are licensed under the
GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
(AGPL-3.0-only). A closed-source product that embeds or links them needs a commercial license.
Mobile apps and brand assets: Proprietary - see
LICENSING.md
Desktop UI built with
Slint
Built by
KeibiSoft SRL
.
By trade
Remote DFIR triage
Mount an evidence share read only across NAT and extract the artifact set you need, with no inbound port, native on Windows, and no kernel driver on the evidence machine. There is a
write-up
and a
DFIR page
.
Post-production handoff
Your footage stays on the studio NAS, and DaVinci Resolve opens it on demand while you travel, with no download or upload to wait for. Click for the two minute demo.
Mount the camera originals
and skip the proxy transcode before the handoff and the relink after it. The
Resolve setup
goes step by step.
Datasets on a rented GPU box
Mount the workstation that holds the data
, with no bucket and no upload before the first batch.
An always-on box, such as a NAS
A session needs both machines online, and a NAS or a home server stays online all the time. The container in
docker/
runs the serving side on that box from plain Docker with the stock kernel. Your laptop mounts the folder from anywhere and reads on demand, so only the bytes a program reads cross the wire. In that run the box, a container on a server in Timisoara, served 161 files to a laptop in Bucharest; after it paired once, the laptop listed the folder and hashed one photo. The setup steps are in
Run it on a NAS
.
Photographers and editors
The raws and the footage stay on the box at the studio. The laptop mounts the folder, Lightroom or Resolve opens the files from the mount, and each file moves only when it is opened; a 1 MiB read out of a big file moves one 16 MiB block. The catalog stays on the laptop, as the
post-production page
and the
video and audio guide
describe. Set the share read only when the box is the archive and the laptop must change nothing.
Agents, and the data they work on
Two agents, one per machine, each drive a KeibiDrop peer through the MCP server. The laptop offers a folder where it sits, and the gpu box mounts it and checksums 24 shards out of 2,184 files six folders deep. In that run 88,581 bytes crossed the network out of 6,784,286 on disk, because that is what it opened. The whole thing, pairing included, took 12.5 seconds.
Build it with
make build-kdmcp
, then
kdmcp install
prints the config snippet for your MCP client. Sending stays off until
KD_SHARE_ROOT
names one directory to send from, so a receiving agent cannot be talked into shipping files out.
Links
Website
Documentation
Compared with sshfs
- measured on a 200 ms link
Compared with other tools
, such as LucidLink, Syncthing, Resilio Sync, rclone, WeTransfer, LocalSend, PairDrop and KDE Connect, one table each

Comparison with alternatives
```

## HN discussion (0 comments)

(no comments)
{"decision": "unsure", "reason": "页面给出了较具体的机制：通过 FUSE 挂载远端文件夹、按 16 MiB 块按需拉取、中继端无法读取的端到端加密，证据足以理解项目。但与 sshfs、LucidLink、rclone 等已有方案相比，差异主要是 NAT 穿透与工程组合，缺少独立验证，也没有 HN 讨论，因此新颖性不足以直接推送。"}

verdict.reasoning: The reason's factual claims are all supported by the page: FUSE-based mounting (macFUSE/fuse3/WinFsp), 16 MiB on-demand blocks, a relay that cannot read the end-to-end encrypted traffic, the comparisons with sshfs, LucidLink and rclone, and zero HN comments. It is specific to this project, and for an unsure decision it names what is missing: independent verification and HN discussion.
